facts.statement: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Fruitadens is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur.

facts.statement: The name Fruitadens means "Fruita teeth", referring to Fruita, Colorado, USA, where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The name means "Fruita teeth", in reference to Fruita, Colorado (USA), where its fossils were first found.

facts.statement: Fruitadens fossils come from at least four individuals of different ages found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado.
facts.quote: It is known from partial skulls and skeletons from at least four individuals of differing biological ages, found in Tithonian (Late Jurassic) rocks of the Morrison Formation in Colorado.

facts.statement: Young adult Fruitadens measured 65 to 75 cm in length and weighed 0.5 to 0.75 kg.
facts.quote: Fruitadens is one of the smallest known ornithischian dinosaurs, with young adults estimated at 65 to 75 cm in length and 0.5 to 0.75 kg in weight.

facts.statement: The hind limb bones of Fruitadens were hollow, similar to those of small theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The hind limb bones were hollow, like those of small theropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Replacement teeth were present in the jaws of Fruitadens, unlike most other heterodontosaurids.
facts.quote: Replacement teeth were present in the jaws, unlike most other heterodontosaurids.

facts.statement: Fruitadens was probably bipedal, cursorial, and omnivorous.
facts.quote: Fruitadens was probably bipedal and cursorial, and is suggested to have been omnivorous.

facts.statement: Fruitadens is the smallest ornithischian in North America, with adults measuring 65 to 75 cm and weighing 0.5 to 0.75 kg.
facts.quote: Fruitadens es el ornitisquio más pequeño de Norteamérica; los adultos medirían de 65 a 75 centímetros y pesarían de 0,5 a 0,75 kilogramos, comparables en tamaño a los dinosaurios más pequeños conocidos, aparte de los pájaros.

facts.statement: Only a small peg-like tooth was present in front of the canine tooth in Fruitadens.
facts.quote: Únicamente un pequeño diente como clavija estaba presente delante del diente canino.

facts.statement: The name Fruitadens comes from Fruita, Colorado, USA, where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: El significado del nombre proviene de Fruita, Colorado, Estados Unidos, donde los fósiles fueron encontrados.

facts.statement: Fruitadens remains were found in the Morrison Formation in Upper Jurassic sediments.
facts.quote: Estos restos se encontraron en la formación Morrison, en sedimentos del Jurásico Superior.

facts.statement: The specimens were found in sandstone beds of the Brushy Basin Member.
facts.quote: Los especímenes se encontraban en lechos de piedra arenisca del Miembro del Bajío Brushy.

facts.statement: The formal description of Fruitadens arrived in 2009, performed by Richard Butler and colleagues.
facts.quote: La descripción formal llegó en 2009, siendo realizada por Richard Butler y colegas.

facts.statement: Fossils called Fruitadens were initially considered a fabrosaurid similar to Echinodon, a genus from the Early Cretaceous of England.
facts.quote: Los fósiles llamados Fruitadens fueron en un principio considerado un fabrosáurido similar a Echinodon, un género del Cretácico Inferior de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: Fruitadens seems to have been more closely related to Heterodontosaurus than to Echinodon, which was closer in time.
facts.quote: Fruitadens parece haber estado más estrechamente vinculado a Heterodontosaurus que a Echinodon, que estaba más cercano en el tiempo.

facts.statement: Four individuals were found at the base of the Morrison Formation in the Bajío Brushy Member, within natural alluvial dikes that deposited sandstones.
facts.quote: Los cuatro individuos se encontraron a en lugares de la base de la formación Morrison en el Miembro Bajío Brushy, en diques naturales de terreno aluvional que habría depositado piedras areniscas.

facts.statement: The Fruita sites preserved a contemporary fauna including snails, clams, crabs, various insects, the lungfish Ceratodus, ray-finned fishes, the turtle Glyptops, rincophidian reptiles Eilenodon and Opisthias, various lizard genera, a mesosuchian crocodylomorph, and the mammals Fruitafossor, Glirodon, and Priacodon.
facts.quote: Los sitios en Fruita preservaron una fauna contemporánea incluyendo caracoles, almejas, cangrejos, varios insectos, representados por rastros fósiles, el pez pulmonado Ceratodus, peces de aletas radiadas, la tortuga Glyptops, reptiles rincocéfalos Eilenodon y Opisthias, varios géneros de lagartos, un cocodrilomorfo mesosuquiano, y los mamíferos Fruitafossor , Glirodon, y Priacodon.

facts.statement: Fruitadens was probably bipedal and is suggested to have been omnivorous, like other heterodontosaurids.
facts.quote: Fruitadens era probablemente bípedo, y como otros heterodontosáuridos se sugiere que habría sido omnívoro.

facts.statement: Like Echinodon and Tianyulong, Fruitadens had less specialized jaws than Early Jurassic heterodontosaurids such as Heterodontosaurus and is interpreted as a generalist feeder.
facts.quote: Como Echinodon y Tianyulong, otros de los últimos heterodontosáuridos, Fruitadens tenían mandíbulas menos especializadas que los de los heterodontosáuridos del Jurásico Inferior como Heterodontosaurus, y se interpreta como un animal de dieta generalista.

facts.statement: A 2012 skull study suggested its diet likely consisted of selective plant material along with insects or other invertebrates.
facts.quote: Un estudio del cráneo publicado en 2012 sugirió que su dieta probablemente estaba compuesta de material vegetal selecto junto a insectos u otros invertebrados.

facts.statement: The genus Fruitadens was named by Butler et al. in 2010.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Fruitadens (genus), Butler et al. 2010

facts.statement: Fruitadens belongs to the family Heterodontosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Heterodontosauridae

facts.statement: Fruitadens is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Fruitadens lived during the Tithonian stage, from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 143.1 million years ago)
